scope: Single paired buffered runs; no streaming or quality gate

runs.text:
(analogy) Comparing retention rates, rather than raw counts, normalizes for the initial size of each group. Think of it like comparing the success rate of two different-sized classes – a higher success rate is more informative than simply knowing the number of students who passed. Retention rate expresses the proportion of individuals who remain over time, allowing for a fairer comparison between groups with different starting points [no course source for this].

What do you think the advantage of using a rate instead of a count would be in a real-world scenario?
